study_identification.title: A neuroimaging measure to capture heterogeneous patterns of atrophy in Parkinson ' s disease and dementia with Lewy bodies

clarity_of_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the purpose of using neuroanatomical normative modelling, defines comparisons (PD vs DLB; high vs low visual performers in PD), and specifies outcomes including total outlier count and associations with cognitive measures. PICO elements are identifiable.
clarity_of_research_objectives.supporting_text: Neuroanatomical normative modelling... Patient-specific atrophy patterns are measured ... (the 'total outlier count'). We aimed to quantify patterns of neurodegenerative dissimilarity in participants with PD and DLB and evaluate the potential clinical relevance of total outlier count by testing its association with key clinical measures...

clear_definition_of_target_population.reason: The study specifies PD and DLB patients from UCL and NACC sites with diagnostic criteria (Queen Square Brain Bank, DLB Consortium), and defines controls with inclusion/exclusion criteria.
clear_definition_of_target_population.supporting_text: ... included 108 participants with PD, 36 with DLB and 38 controls ... diagnosed as having PD or probable DLB if they satisfied Queen Square Brain Bank PD diagnostic criteria ... and the Dementia with Lewy Bodies Consortium Criteria ... Controls ... Inclusion criteria were being aged 50-80 and exclusions were ...

clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_crite.reason: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are detailed for both UCL and NACC cohorts, including age range for controls and specific diagnostic requirements; exclusions include TBI and co-morbid disorders; PD dementia excluded by MDS criteria.
clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_crite.supporting_text: Exclusions were a history of traumatic brain injury, or major co-morbid psychiatric or confounding neurological disorders; and for participants with PD, presence of dementia was also an exclusion criterion, defined using Movement Disorder Society criteria ... Inclusion criteria were being aged 50-80 ... Participants from site '8361' ... met ... 1) dementia diagnosis; 2) ... Lewy body disease; ... 4) absence of a diagnosis of PD.

validity_of_normative_modeling_outcome_m.reason: The outcome measures are clearly defined: regional cortical thickness and subcortical volumes processed via FreeSurfer; z-scores relative to a large reference cohort; binarization at a defined threshold; aggregation across 169 regions to compute total outlier count.
validity_of_normative_modeling_outcome_m.supporting_text: ... generated z-scores from T1w-MRI ... relative to normative regional cortical thickness and subcortical volumes ... Outliers (z < -1.96) were aggregated across 169 brain regions per participant ... The total number of outliers across the 169 regions (148 cortical and 21 subcortical) was summed per participant to provide the total outlier count.

handling_of_confounding_variables.reason: The normative models include age and sex as covariates and account for site differences; the statistical analyses adjust for age and sex; transfer learning recalibrates models using site-specific controls to handle scanner/site effects.
handling_of_confounding_variables.supporting_text: ... using a warped Bayesian Linear Regression with age and sex as covariates, and accounting for site differences ... The reference normative model was recalibrated ... to account for residual differences in data distributions, caused by factors such as scanner differences. ... Linear regressions, correcting for age and sex, were used ...

clarity_of_data_sources.reason: Data sources are clearly identified: UCL site cohort and NACC ADRC '8361' site, with recruitment context and criteria for inclusion.
clarity_of_data_sources.supporting_text: Structural T1w-MRI data from two sites were used ... University College London (UCL) ... The second site was the pseudoanonymised Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center (ADRC) '8361' which contributes data to the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (NACC) database ...

description_of_image_acquisition_protoco.reason: Scanner manufacturer, field strength, sequence, coil, and key acquisition parameters (voxel size, TE, TR, flip angle, duration) are provided for UCL scans; NACC scanners noted as 1.5T GE with parameters available via database.
description_of_image_acquisition_protoco.supporting_text: Structural T1w-MRI scans at UCL were acquired on a 3 T Siemens Magnetom Prisma ... MPRAGE ... 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxel, TE = 3.34 ms, TR = 2530 ms, flip angle = 7°, acquisition time = 9 min. Structural T1w-MRI scans from NACC ADRC '8361' were acquired on 1.5 T GE scanners ...

details_of_data_preprocessing.reason: Processing pipeline and software are specified: FreeSurfer v6.0.0 recon-all; Destrieux parcellation; aseg subcortical volumes; manual QC by visual inspection.
details_of_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: The 'recon-all' function in FreeSurfer v6.0.0 ... Cortical thickness values (Destrieux parcellation ... ) and subcortical volumes (aseg.stats) were extracted. Processed images were quality controlled by visually inspecting grey and white matter boundaries ...

clarity_of_data_partitioning_methods.reason: No train/validation/test partitioning was performed; a pre-trained reference normative model was recalibrated using control data from the study sites, and analyses consisted of group comparisons and associations.
clarity_of_data_partitioning_methods.supporting_text: The reference normative model was recalibrated to the study datasets with an adapted transfer learning approach ... inputting control data from our two study sites ... Z-scores were then generated ...

details_of_normative_modeling_approach.reason: Model type (warped Bayesian Linear Regression), covariates (age, sex), site effects handling, reference cohort size, recalibration via transfer learning, and software (PCNToolkit v0.20) are described.
details_of_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: ... using a warped Bayesian Linear Regression with age and sex as covariates, and accounting for site differences ... reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites ... The reference normative model was recalibrated ... using ... controls ... All modelling steps were performed using PCNToolkit (v0.20).

details_of_training_algorithm.reason: The study did not train models from scratch; it used an existing reference normative model and recalibrated it. Therefore optimization algorithms, epochs, or convergence criteria are not applicable.
details_of_training_algorithm.supporting_text: The reference normative model was recalibrated to the study datasets with an adapted transfer learning approach ...

model_performance_evaluation_metrics.reason: The paper reports statistical results for associations and group comparisons (e.g., beta coefficients, t-statistics, p-values) but does not report normative model performance metrics such as EV, MSLL, R², or correlation between predicted and observed values.
model_performance_evaluation_metrics.supporting_text: Examples of reported statistics: 'β = -4.73 (SE = 1.30); t = -3.64; p < 0.01' ... No sections report EV/MSLL/R² for the normative models.

implementation_of_internal_validation.reason: There is no description of internal validation procedures (e.g., held-out validation, cross-validation) specific to the normative modeling pipeline within the study data.
implementation_of_internal_validation.supporting_text: Methods focus on recalibration using controls and subsequent analyses; no cross-validation or internal validation procedure is described.

external_data_validation.reason: Although analyses included participants from two sites (UCL and NACC), there is no dedicated external validation of model performance on an independent dataset; both sites were used for recalibration and main analyses.
external_data_validation.supporting_text: Structural T1w-MRI data from two sites were used ... subgroup analyses compared DLB participants at the UCL and NACC sites ... (not an external validation of model performance).

description_of_dataset_characteristics.reason: Sample sizes for groups and sites are reported; demographics and clinical characteristics are summarized with means/SDs and group comparisons (with a table referenced).
description_of_dataset_characteristics.supporting_text: We included 108 participants with PD and 61 with DLB ... plus 165 controls ... see Table 1 for demographic and clinical information ...

performance_metrics_and_statistical_unce.reason: The paper reports point estimates (means, beta coefficients), standard errors, t-statistics, and p-values, but does not report confidence intervals or Bayesian credible intervals for key estimates.
performance_metrics_and_statistical_unce.supporting_text: Examples include 'mean = 8.7 (SD = 11.3)' and 'β = -5.60 (SE = 1.74); t = -3.23; p < 0.01'; confidence intervals are not provided.

consideration_for_reproducibility.reason: Software versions are reported (FreeSurfer v6.0.0; PCNToolkit v0.20), and data sources are identified (NACC ADRC site), but there is no explicit code release or trained model sharing described in the provided text.
consideration_for_reproducibility.supporting_text: All modelling steps were performed using PCNToolkit (v0.20) ... The 'recon-all' function in FreeSurfer v6.0.0 was used ...

interpretation_specific_to_normative_mod.reason: They interpret individual-level deviation patterns via total outlier counts, compare dissimilarity using Hamming distances, and discuss associations with cognitive measures, emphasizing potential clinical relevance.
interpretation_specific_to_normative_mod.supporting_text: ... measured objectively and summarised to index overall neurodegeneration (the 'total outlier count') ... Hamming distance ... Higher total outlier counts were associated with poorer MoCA ... and composite cognitive scores ...

additional_comments.additional_comments: Supplementary material confirms robustness of findings using a more liberal outlier threshold (z < -1.282) and reports dissimilarity (Hamming distance) differences by group. See materials/1-s2.0-S2213158224000354-mmc1.md (Replication analysis using more liberal threshold).
